notes.title: Devlog #12: Prequel
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone! This devlog will be more about the plans for Kingso and the achievements of indie development in general.[/p][p]It has been about 100 days since the release of the largest Kingso update. During this time, I started working on a new project — CaveVox, a prequel to Kingso. It is a 3D voxel roguelike set in a fantasy medieval dungeon. Unlike Kingso, where you explored the continent of Avelir in 2D, now you will be able to descend into the depths of one of the equally detailed dungeons in 3D.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What awaits you in CaveVox?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Unique dungeon generation[/b] — each dungeon level has its own style but is always unique. This applies to appearance, objects, interactions, and monsters.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Spatial sound and a living dungeon atmosphere[/b] — you can hear the sounds of monsters and the environment.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Combat system and diverse monster behavior[/b] — monsters have different behaviors, can form groups or attack alone, and have hearing and sight.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cooperative mode[/b] — it is planned that you will be able to descend alone or with friends into the dungeon and play your role in your own journey.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Permanent death[/b] — as in Kingso, each character is unique and can be lost at any moment.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Classless progression[/b] — create a character according to your own play style.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Atmospheric details:[/b] dust, cobwebs, vines, broken objects, traps, the ability to extinguish torches, and much more.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/3e3f8378633066152b3ad98dbd57aa4ce1848cc9.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/f3072f648d857e46096373a51649b3747c121dae.png"][/img][/p][p]In terms of graphics, CaveVox combines simple pixel stylization with detailed lighting and shadow effects. Each level will differ: from well-kept halls to ruined and overgrown dungeons.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What’s new in Kingso?[/b][/p][p]Work on Kingso continues as well! Planned features include:[/p][list][*][p]More monsters for different biomes and their movement across the map[/p][/*][*][p]New types of quests from the Adventurers’ Guild[/p][/*][*][p]Economy system and caravans[/p][/*][*][p]New animations and interactions with characters[/p][/*][*][p]More story and regular dialogues[/p][/*][*][p]Code optimization, graphics improvement, and addition of atmospheric details.[/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you for reading this devlog. Your reaction and support are very important to me! I am looking forward to seeing you at the demo release in October 2025 and the early access release of CaveVox in Q4 2025![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3942210/CaveVox_Demo/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]You can also join the official CaveVox [url="https://discord.gg/YPqBB68w9N"]Discord server[/url].[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #11: Progress Update
notes.notes:
[h3]Introduction[/h3]

Hello, adventurers!

In this devlog, we’re sharing a general development progress report. Much has changed in Kingso since the last devlog - systems became deeper, visuals more expressive, and the world more dynamic.

[h3]What’s New[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Biomes:[/b]
Water movement, animated environments, and more immersive ambiance across regions.
[*][b]Domains:[/b]
Around 30 nations and 200 territories now shape the continent’s political and cultural landscape.
[*][b]Creatures:[/b]
At this stage, only slimes are implemented - various types adapted to different environments. Despite their simplicity, they already feature distinct habitats, behaviors, and stats. This lays the foundation for a richer creature ecosystem in future updates.
[*][b]Dialogues:[/b]
Visual elements such as character portraits, background art, and dynamic text flow are now fully implemented. Choices affect interaction outcomes.
[*][b]Quests:[/b]
The Adventurer’s Guild is now functional. Players can accept and complete tasks, build squads, and explore the world.
[*][b]Saving System:[/b]
The core mechanic - one life. Autosaves are now active and bind tightly to the player’s progression.
[*][b]Sound Effects (SFX):[/b]
Interface sounds and ambient game world audio now provide a more responsive and atmospheric experience.
[*][b]Settings:[/b]
Added support for 15 major languages, with plans to expand localization in future updates. A basic control guide is now available to help new players get started. Additionally, new settings have been introduced for audio and rendering, allowing for better customization of the experience.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/cbc657f1e2bfa6c2d09c904bf097b04e71b4c160.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/51d6f44b3700a8ee6698f6790cd91d694b2014a3.png[/img]

[h3]What’s next?[/h3]
Quite a lot will be expanded in upcoming updates. The world of Kingso is turning into a rich, multi-layered experience with meaningful exploration and storytelling.

This version is already playable - players can explore the continent and complete guild quests.

Future updates will focus on expanding gameplay beyond combat, squads, and quests, introducing mechanics that enhance freedom of choice and personal storytelling.

[previewyoutube=9MpVjRkS2qs;full][/previewyoutube]

Thank you for reading this Devlog!

notes.title: Devlog #10: Game World
notes.notes:
[b]Introduction[/b]

Hello everyone, today we're going to talk about the story of Kingso. The game itself offers different playstyles, and the story is more of an additional element that describes the world of the continent of Avelir. You'll be able to choose your own path in the game, and this is what makes the story unconventional in the traditional sense: there is no predefined "correct" ending.

[b]Story[/b]

Avelir, once a prosperous continent, experienced the greatest catastrophe in its history. A magical cataclysm destroyed the old great kingdoms, disrupted the balance of power, and freed ancient forces that are once again interfering with the fate of mankind.

By the time of the game, Avelir is:

[list]
[*] Fragmented lands where dozens of kingdoms, factions, and orders vie for power;
[*] Pirates, shadowy alliances, thieves, and mercenaries weaving their own intrigues;
[*] Ruthless lands: from the snow-covered northern peaks to the impassable swamps and forests;
[*] The chance to influence the future of the world through actions, decisions, and alliances.
[/list]
The world of Avelir is harsh and unpredictable: even powerful kingdoms are susceptible to betrayals, uprisings, and secret alliances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/5f0e9de5338d32453f2ee5eb92701934b4207d8a.png[/img]

[b]The Player's Role and Goals[/b]

In Kingso, you are not a passive observer. The world does not exist for you; you are a participant in it. Your character is an outsider: a person from another world, mysteriously thrown into Avelir. You only have one life in the game. If your hero or companion dies, there will be no second chance. You may be lucky to survive the blows of fate, but the cost of a mistake is absolute.

You will begin your journey without influence, without allies, and without knowledge of the world. You will need to earn reputation, find companions, fight monsters, and sometimes – survive at all costs.

In this world, only those who can see more than meets the eye succeed. Every choice has a price. Sometimes an irreversible one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/fcb59c069a3c7e69af48f11d7208375da9eef253.png[/img]

[b]A Living World[/b]

Avelir is not a static backdrop. While you explore the world, life continues around you:

[list]
[*] Factions form alliances and wage wars independently of you;
[*] Pirates and monsters raid and attack;
[*] Rumors and events arise from actions – even without your involvement.
[/list]
The world of Avelir continues to live, change, and fight for the future. The living Avelir does not forgive those who live in the past. Today, a neutral faction may become your sworn enemy tomorrow. And a random event at the other end of the continent can ruin everything you've built.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/005f716c74bfe8d516ccb8116d269ffe81a4c175.png[/img]

[b]Conclusion[/b]

To wrap up, I want to talk about the price of Kingso. The game used to cost only 1 dollar in the earliest stages of development. The goal back then was clear: to make the project accessible to everyone and gradually develop it together with the community.

Today, Kingso costs 4 dollars, and this is completely justified. This price is directly tied to the increase in the quality of the game. At the moment, it is the only game in the world that combines a fantasy-medieval setting, a unique graphic style, and a large-scale development of gameplay mechanics.

By purchasing Kingso once, you get access to the full final version of the game and all future updates without any additional purchases, DLC, or season passes. No hidden costs – only the development and growth of the project. If you haven’t discovered some game mechanics yet, don’t worry: everything mentioned in updates will be added, it just takes time.

Kingso is a unique work in its genre and quality. I sincerely hope that you will feel the care and effort put into this world. The game will only continue to flourish with each new update.

Thank you for reading this Devlog!

notes.title: Devlog #9: Battles and Squads
notes.notes:
Introduction

Hello everyone! In this devlog, we’ll talk about battles in Kingso.

In the previous devlog, we already mentioned that the game map is quite vast. Exploring the entire map will take a significant amount of in-game time. The idea is that each biome and nation will differ not only visually but also in terms of gameplay. Over time, the game will become increasingly diverse.

Squads

Battles in Kingso are a feature that was previously missing and much needed. After all, what kind of fantasy world would it be without enemies? As you journey through the uncharted fantasy continent of Avelir, you may encounter friendly, neutral, or hostile entities. These could be other travelers, caravans, lords, or monster-infested zones.

Ordinary beings will develop city economies, wage wars, and defend their territories. Monsters, however, are a separate gameplay mechanic. The idea is that players won’t only encounter enemies by chance, but can also join an adventurers’ guild and deliberately hunt monsters - rising in rank, earning rewards, and developing their squad.

Your goals depend entirely on your choices and playstyle. But it’s important to understand that this is a strategic endeavor. You’ll need to decide how many companions to recruit, how to develop them, and thereby shape the story of your journey.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/be9877c7df48a6dbc4d4bc2973fe4573d2aea8e7.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/98ab120039f6978ea15fb0102abe6084035676c8.png[/img]

Combat

Let’s say you spot a group of small blue slimes and decide to smash them. Sometimes you can see the number of enemies in an opposing squad ahead of time, which helps you assess your chances. Usually, if you’re in an adventurers' guild, that intel is provided in advance based on your quest and rank.

To initiate combat, you need to move into the enemy’s tile. This transitions you from the global map to the battle area. You won’t always know which side of the battlefield you or the enemy will start on, but the terrain is always known in advance - it is copied exactly from the global map. For example, if the battle happens over water, your movement toward the enemy will be slower. You may also randomly alter the arrangement of your units. That’s why it’s important to consider not only large-scale strategy but also small details like how many arrows your archers have, your character’s upgrades, your squad’s level, and more.

[previewyoutube=ZipsB7YU2GU;full][/previewyoutube]

In the future, we plan to add direct control over battles, allowing players to command characters themselves. For now, battles are fun to watch, and it’s exciting to build and develop your squad.

Thank you for reading this devlog! Next time, we’ll talk about the storyline and the game’s continent, diving even deeper into its world.

notes.title: Devlog #8: Continent and Biomes
notes.notes:
[b]Introduction[/b]

Hello everyone!

Previous articles mostly covered the general development of the game. Now, with a major update on the horizon - and going forward in general - devlogs will be published across multiple platforms to keep you informed about what's changing in Kingso. In the last article, I talked about the game engine and how Kingso evolved into its current form. Today, we’re continuing that topic — this time focusing on the central arena of all in-game activity: the world map.

[b]Map Structure[/b]

Kingso is built on a tile-based map system. When the game ran on a custom engine, everything was managed directly with minimal abstraction. However, after transitioning to Godot and integrating through the TileMapLayer, our approach became more modular and flexible. This opened up new possibilities, but also introduced a set of unique challenges.

There aren’t many games in the industry that combine a classic top-down view with a massive open world and multi-layered tile maps. Even after two years of development, the only remotely similar example we came across was Civilization 1991. Still, Kingso follows its own path - its visual style is far more vibrant and “alive” with a rich atmosphere, detailed environments, and visual effects that create the sense of a breathing, dynamic world.

[b]Optimization and Performance[/b]

Building such a world isn't just a matter of design - it’s a serious performance challenge. Imagine hundreds of thousands of tiles, each potentially having multiple layers, unique properties, and interactions. To make this run smoothly, you need to use batch rendering, which allows efficient use of the GPU by drawing everything in groups.

But rendering is only part of the equation. The world is expected to feel alive, which means implementing many systems - character movement, environmental interaction, object behaviors, and more. In order to handle this complexity without performance loss, it becomes essential to apply prediction and filtering algorithms that reduce real-time computation, especially by focusing on areas near the player. These techniques help maintain a sense of scale without sacrificing responsiveness.

[b]World Scale and Structure[/b]

As of now, the world map in Kingso includes around 30 nations, over 200 unique regions, and a wide variety of biomes and environmental elements. The map is constructed from multiple layered tilemaps, with each layer representing distinct aspects such as terrain, vegetation, infrastructure, and more.

While the map itself doesn't simulate climate directly, the world is divided into climatic zones - such as dry regions, humid lowlands, swampy areas, or snowy landscapes. These zones influence the type of flora found in each area. Some trees, for instance, grow only in colder regions, while others require high humidity. As players explore the continent, they will notice natural transitions between these zones, reinforcing the feeling of a vast and diverse world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/e6b46692194cc2e2fef02f9250b3148a57241863.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/e0350413fd72a7c449b91342e8949ff1179785a2.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38534801/fa2a944add3d602dcf20d1ba8c359e002b2c5cab.jpg[/img]

[b]Part of the narrative[/b]

Despite its fantasy foundation, we strive for realism in the details. Each biome affects not only the visual appearance, but also gameplay - influencing enemy types, characters behavior, available resources, survival conditions, and much more. Traveling across the continent becomes more than a change of scenery - it’s a true act of exploration, with meaningful consequences.

Thank you for reading this article!

notes.title: New biomes, improved graphics, animation and interfaces
notes.notes:
We continue to develop the game and are happy to share the latest changes.

[b]New biomes[/b]
Unique biomes have been added to the game, each of which has its own atmosphere and style. Now the world will become even more diverse and interesting to explore. In the future, each type of biome will be increasingly emphasized in the gameplay.

[b]Improved graphics[/b]
The graphic design has received a significant update. We've chosen the final graphics style, reworked textures, and added more details to make the gameplay more immersive.

[b]Animation of static objects[/b]
To create a living and realistic world, we added animation to previously static objects.
This makes the gameplay more dynamic and rich.

[b]Guild, squad and inventory interfaces[/b]
Work has begun on the guild, squad management, and inventory systems. These elements will provide players with a convenient way to interact with allies and equipment.

[b]Combat system[/b]
The combat system is currently under active development and is already half complete. Experience controlled, real-time battles with a variety of strategic options.

We strive to make the gaming experience as immersive as possible and thank you for your patience and support. There are still many innovations ahead!

notes.title: Getting Back on Track
notes.notes:
Dear Steam Gaming Community!

We want to sincerely apologize for the long absence of updates and news about our game. It was difficult for us to make a decision to review our approach to supporting the game, but we are convinced that this is a necessary step towards future success.

With great joy, we inform you that now we are fully focused on updating the game! To achieve this, we have switched to the new Godot 4.3 engine. For a long time, we were developing our own engine, but over time, we realized that Godot is just as good, and even better. During the migration process, almost all existing content, graphics, and functions from old game versions were transferred.

Work is being carried out intensively, and we are very hopeful that you will see the results of our efforts. We will inform you about updates and progress as they are achieved, so that you are always kept informed.

Thank you for your support and patience!

notes.title: About developing Kingso and porting to our new engine
notes.notes:
Hello friends! We are excited to share with you some news about what we've been up to lately. As always, we strive to be as productive as possible and never stop at what we've already achieved. Over the past period, we've dedicated a lot of attention to developing several of our projects.

We aim to create games that are exciting and interesting for our users. To achieve this goal, we're constantly improving our technological base, enhancing graphics and sound, and adding new features and functionalities.

We can't reveal all the details about our projects, but we can confidently say that our games will be worthy of your time and attention. In total, we're working on about seven projects of varying complexity, including games of different genres and directions. We're sure that you'll enjoy them and will keep coming back to them again and again.

Currently, two projects are being actively developed. One of them is a turn-based strategy game called Kingso, which is one of our main projects. We pay special attention to it, as we are confident in its potential and expect great success from it.

Given the scale of our projects, we plan to release them gradually as they become ready for release or first showcases for players.

Developing such a quantity of projects certainly takes a lot of time and energy from our team. However, we believe that this approach gives us the necessary experience and knowledge in different areas of game development. Over time, we plan to expand our team by attracting experienced developers and using better development methods to make our games even better.

Regarding Lacuna Engine and Kingso.
As stated in our earlier articles, we are porting the game to our own new engine. This is because the previous versions of the game were simply entangled with the engine itself and its system, and turned into the game. Even the fact that the code was divided into modules and well optimized does not solve all the accumulated problems. Understanding all the shortcomings of the engine and the problems with the planned network mode, work on our own engine was started. As we developed our engine, we encountered unforeseen difficulties that had to be solved as they arose. For example, we had to completely rewrite many algorithms because they did not work on the new engine. We also had to delve into the study of some technologies, which took quite a lot of time.

As of April 2023, the following has been done in the engine:
[list]
[*] Initial interface/icons, program style and design;
[*] Debugging system using Script Output and Log;
[*] Resource loading system, called Import System + engine file types;
[*] Lua (luajit) code system;
[*] Custom render (also possible to run the game separately from the engine).
[/list]
Currently in development:
[list]
[*] Kings0 is being actively and easily ported to the new engine (~50% ported);
[*] Interface is being refined + gradually creating a plugin system for the engine;
[*] NodeEditor editors are being created;
[*] Support for network development in two modes (Own server or Local network).
[/list]
Planned for the future:
[list]
[*] Simplify code development on the engine in favor of visual programming;
[*] Port Kings0 and maintain its updates, as well as start developing other projects on it.
[/list]
I think this gives an idea of the scale of the work done and planned for the future. If you have any suggestions, wishes, or feedback, please write to us, we try to respond to everyone. Thank you very much for your support and interest in our work. We will continue to work on creating quality games for you!
